title: perf-canary: improved auto-detection thresholds and rollout guards (hysteresis + KV-aware)
author: Priya Raman
description:
Context:
This PR improves the performance canary's automated regression detection and rollout guards. Over the last month we've seen noisy alerts from the canary on short-lived latency spikes and a recent incident where a model rollout proceeded even though throughput regressed under certain KV-cache-heavy workloads.

Goals:
- Reduce false positives by adding adaptive hysteresis to threshold checks.
- Make detection KV-cache aware: separate steady-state latency/throughput checks for cold vs warm KV cache buckets.
- Add conservative rollout guards that block automatic canary-based rollouts when sustained regressions or high variance are detected.
- Add integration tests and perf-canary e2e harness to surface regressions in CI.

What changed (high-level):
- detector/auto_detect.py: rewrote thresholding logic to include a two-window hysteresis (short window for quick signals, long window for confirmation) and adaptive thresholds based on historical variance.
- detector/kv_bucket.py: new module to tag traces/metrics by KV-cache state (cold/warm/partial).
- rollout/guards.py: added GuardEvaluator that reasons over decay windows, variance, and KV-bucket split to decide allow/hold/rollback decisions.
- perf-canary/ci_harness: added an e2e job that runs synthetic KV cold/warm traces against the canary and validates guard behavior.
- observability: added per-bucket histograms and a dashboard JSON example for SLO teams.
- tests: unit tests for hysteresis logic, KV classification, and two integration tests covering a synthetic throughput regression and a transient spike.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector hysteresis implemented and tested
- [x] KV-bucket tagging and metrics emitted
- [x] GuardEvaluator added with allow/hold/rollback outcomes
- [x] CI perf harness job + sample traces
- [x] Docs: rollout guard README and notes in perf-canary.md
- [x] Feature flagged behind runtime.canary.autodetect_v2

Rationale and tradeoffs:
- We chose a two-window hysteresis instead of a single threshold to balance sensitivity and stability; short window catches regressions quickly while the long window prevents flapping.
- Splitting metrics by KV-cache state avoids conflating cold-start latency with steady-state regressions, but it introduces more metrics to track. We emit per-bucket histograms and a composite signal for teams that prefer a single indicator.
- Guards are intentionally conservative for auto-rollouts; manual rollouts can still proceed with operator acknowledgement.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on detector/auto_detect.py and rollout/guards.py for correctness and potential perf implications. The change is behind a feature flag and rollout-controlled.
- I ran local perf harnesses against a small GPU cluster; results included in the CI job artifacts.

Related: ENG-1428 (auto-detect improvements), ENG-1509 (rollout guard design doc).
